rationale: Round 0 compiled and ran correctly, so this round pushes security harder while keeping cost penalties moderate. SUB gets the highest SecurityGain since arithmetic substitution is cheap, low-risk, and effective on the integer-heavy Ocean simulation loops (movement, neighbor counting); its cost weights stay low so it applies broadly. BCF and IBR carry high SecurityGain to frustrate static control-flow recovery and disassembly-based analysis, but their RuntimeCost penalties (0.45/0.30) are raised above round 0 because Ocean is simulation-like with hot nested loops and BCF in particular multiplies loop-body costs; SizeCost for BCF is tempered by the tiny 3.7KB text section, which has room to grow. FLA keeps a strong SecurityGain for the five largest functions (~300 bytes each, real control-flow to flatten) but carries the highest SizeCost weight (0.55) since flattening small trivial accessors inflates them without benefit. SPLIT is retained mostly for DiversityGain and as a synergy pass that feeds FLA/IBR more basic blocks to transform; it is nearly free. ICALL is weighted strongly for DiversityGain since C++ virtual-style dispatch and function pointers in this benchmark give indirect-call conversion good coverage, with a moderate RuntimeCost penalty for indirect-branch predictor pressure in the simulation loop. IGV stays mid-range: opaque global state adds analysis burden but its CorrectnessRisk weight is the highest here to keep it off functions with observable global side effects.
